newsitem.title: FRANCE: Nestle's Perrier launches youthful drink.
newsitem.headline: Nestle's Perrier launches youthful drink.

text.p: Perrier-Vittel, the French mineral water unit of Swiss food and drink group Nestle, said on Wednesday its first foray into the soft drinks market would target the important youth segment.
"Perrier decided to attack the soft drink market because it wanted to have a product which targeted young people," Arnaud Collas, product manager for the new drink told Reuters.
"Perrier (mineral water) is mostly consumed by the over 25s. We needed a product which touches 15-25 year-olds," he added.

The new drink "Fu", which is made from Perrier mineral water, sugar and secret natural plant extracts, was launched this month in cafes, bars, bistros and service stations in France and in food shops in Belgium.

A national poster campaign in France, run by Publicis SA unit Loeb et Associes, showing teenagers desperate to get their hands on a dose of Fu as if it were a drug, ended its first two-week run on Wednesday and will run for another two weeks from August 6-13.
Fu, which is pronounced like the French word for 'crazy' (fou), comes in dark blue cans or 33cl Perrier bottles labelled with the word "Fu" in Oriental-style lettering in acid yellow.
"It is an unusual drink, it is not like anything else," said Marc Loeb, chairman of Loeb et Associes.
He and Collas said the poster campaign was designed to convey the message that once you have tasted Fu, you're hooked.
"You start to like it, then you can't do without it," Loeb said.
Perrier is using its parenthood of Fu to give the new drink legitimacy. The bottled version looks like a jazzed-up Perrier with the familiar green bottle made darkened by the brown Fu liquid.
The name also has strong associations with Perrier's long time French advertising campaign slogan, "Perrier - c'est fou!" (Perrier's crazy!).
"For years the slogan was the Perrier brand's advertising territory. It (Fu) is a way of marking Perrier's paternity," Loeb said.
"The Perrier name is very well-known. People trust it," Collas said.
Collas declined to give sales or market share targets for Fu, or to specify when Perrier might launch it into the food retailing circuit or in other countries.
